readme.html:
Evaluate and improve AI agent skills and plugins: quality, security, overlap, compatibility, and real impact across agents

📺 Livestream: Ask the Experts: Evaluating Agent Skills

SkillEvaluator checks AI agent skills and plugins, and measures a skill's effect on task results: start with quality checks, then compare runs with and without a skill.

Agent skills are folders of instructions and supporting files defined by the Agent Skills specification. SkillEvaluator is part of the NVIDIA Verified Skills pipeline.

Get started

Check skills from your terminal, CI, or agent.

1. Run the CLI directly 2. Add it to your repo via CI 3. Wire it to your agent

Install with pip:

pip install skillevaluator
Or install with uv
uv tool install \
  skillevaluator

Then check your skill, no key:

skillevaluator validate \
  ./my-skill --tiers 1

Other tiers: installation guide.

Our CI template checks every skill change. No evaluation code to maintain.

Run this in your GitHub repository. It opens a setup PR:

skillevaluator ci init

GitLab details: repository guide.

Add the skill to Claude Code, Codex or another agent:

npx skills add \
  NVIDIA/SkillEvaluator

Then ask: "Is my skill any good?" See the agent guide.

⚡ Harness check: will your agent load your skill? Know in seconds.

No LLM inference · No model key · No agent run

skillevaluator harness-check ./my-skill

╭─ Harness compatibility · my-skill ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
│  ⚠️ codex        degraded    Description cut to 1,021 chars + '...' in the skill list   │
│  ❌ claude-code  not loaded  .agents/skills is not scanned                              │
│  ✅ opencode     loads                                                                  │
│  ✅ hermes       loads                                                                  │
│  ✅ openclaw     loads                                                                  │
│  ❌ copilot-cli  not loaded  description is 1,028 UTF-16 units, 4 over the 1,024 limit  │
╰────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── ❌ 2 of 6 not loaded ─╯

validate above runs it by default, as part of Tier 1. 🧪 Ready to go deeper? Try a live agent evaluation (Tier 3).

Quickstart

Both use bundled text-analyzer.

Start here Requires First result
Run without an LLM Git and uv A deterministic quality score and findings
Use NVIDIA Build Git, uv, and a Build API key Model-backed rubric scores and feedback

Install uv and Git, then get the example:

git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/NVIDIA/SkillEvaluator.git
cd SkillEvaluator

uv provisions Python 3.13 and dependencies.

Run without an LLM

uv run --python 3.13 skillevaluator quality-check \
  src/skillevaluator/tier3/reference_skills/text-analyzer \
  -r cli -r json -o reports/first-quality

No API key, scanner, GPU or Docker is needed. The example scores 88.8/100 (B), exits 0 and saves reports/first-quality/skillevaluator-quality.json. The passing threshold defaults to 70.

This checks static quality; publication evidence stays INCOMPLETE. Security needs scanners; agent impact needs live evaluation. Replace the example path with your skill directory. See the keyless walkthrough.

Use NVIDIA Build

Eligible NVIDIA Developer Program members can use NVIDIA-hosted endpoints for free prototyping, subject to access terms and rate limits.

  1. Sign in at build.nvidia.com and complete enrollment.
  2. Open a model page, select Get API Key, and generate your key.
  3. Set the provider and key in the same terminal, then run the rubric check:
export SKILL_EVAL_LLM_PROVIDER=nv_build
export NVIDIA_API_KEY='nvapi-...'
uv run --python 3.13 --extra llm skillevaluator rubric-eval \
  src/skillevaluator/tier3/reference_skills/text-analyzer \
  -r cli -r json -o reports/first-build

The command sends skill documentation to the model and saves feedback in reports/first-build/skillevaluator-rubric.json. No agent runtime or Docker is needed. Completed evaluations can still fail rubric thresholds.

The same key supports Tier 2 embeddings and supported Tier 3 agents. See the Build walkthrough or provider configuration.

Three-tier overview

Each tier is independent. Add its extra to your command:

Tier Question Example after setup Additional setup
Tier 1: Validation Is the skill safe, well-formed and harness-compatible? uv run skillevaluator tier1 ./my-skill --no-llm External scanners for full static coverage; a provider and model clients enable LLM checks
Tier 2: Deduplication Does guidance repeat or overlap? uv run --extra tier2 skillevaluator tier2 ./my-skill Embeddings and chat; add --catalog ./skill-catalog.json for inter-skill comparison
Tier 3: Live Evaluation Does the skill help the agent? uv run --extra tier3 skillevaluator tier3 ./my-skill Provider access, a supported agent, and a running sandbox (Docker by default)

Tier 1 fetches pinned, verified SkillSpector and Gitleaks releases when they are missing; Semgrep is optional. See scanners. --no-llm does not remove scanner requirements; a scanner that cannot run is INCOMPLETE and exits nonzero. SkillSpector provides specialized skill security scanning; Harbor, the open-source agent evaluation framework, powers sandboxed agent runs.

Tier 2 reports when inter-skill comparison did not run. Tier 3 autopilot reuses sources or creates one skill-grounded case with limited coverage. See tier guides.

Run the combined pipeline

After setting up the provider, scanners, and agent sandbox, run all three tiers:

uv run --python 3.13 --extra all skillevaluator doctor --env-mode docker
uv run --python 3.13 --extra all skillevaluator validate ./my-skill

doctor checks readiness, not inference success. validate runs all tiers with autopilot for skills. Use --tiers 1,2 to skip live evaluation or --tiers 1 for static checks. --no-autopilot requires an existing source. Other artifact types retain their applicable stages.

Tier 1 gates validate. Tier 2 gates unless --no-block-on-dedup is set; Tier 3 gates only with --block-on-agent-eval. Model and managed-sandbox usage can incur charges; see runtime and cost.

Standalone generation needs substantive evals/EVAL.md guidance, a --prompt file with task requests and outcomes, or matching retained traces. --force below replaces the autopilot starter; --refine refines it. Explicit --grounding skill permits skill-only starters. Review cases; templates omit unauthored negatives.

uv run --python 3.13 --extra tier3 skillevaluator tier3 create-eval-dataset ./my-skill --full --prompt eval-guidance.md --force

Run from a source checkout

Prefix commands with uv run --python 3.13; see extras.

Research and citation

Resources: paper, PDF, DOI, BibTeX, and NVIDIA Developer blog. Cite the paper and record the SkillEvaluator release or commit; see CITATION.cff.

Documentation

See the documentation for setup, tier guides, reports, CI integration, CLI reference, and performance dashboard.

Installation and third-party software

This project will download and install additional third-party open source software projects. Review the license terms of these open source projects before use.

Contributing

Read CONTRIBUTING.md and run:

make lint && make test && make build

See project governance and Code of Conduct.

Support

Support level: Experimental. Community-supported, best-effort, with no SLA or NVIDIA enterprise support entitlement. Report bugs and feature requests through GitHub Issues; see SUPPORT.md.

Security

Report suspected vulnerabilities using the private process in SECURITY.md. Do not disclose security issues in a public GitHub issue.
